patch.value: Lifecycle field-completeness contract: each item type declares the fields required at each status transition, machine-checked by pm validate

Best-practice PM structure exists only by convention: Epics carry charters, Stories carry persona-goal-benefit, Decisions carry context/options/consequences, Features carry acceptance criteria, closed items carry resolution evidence — but pm validate checks only close-time resolution fields (pm-wenq) and nothing else. Define a per-type, per-transition field-completeness contract as schema data (not hardcoded): type X moving to status Y requires/expects fields Z, with warn vs require per governance policy. Validate gains a --check-completeness class reporting per-type violations; CI rides the pm-kpftft ratchet so completeness only improves. Schema customization (pm-8jdc) lets projects extend the contract for custom types; the GA contract (pm-xp1xsw) publishes the built-in defaults. This is what turns 'well-defined pm items' from a social norm into a checked invariant, and it gives the context engine (pm-4k6b) a machine-readable knowledge-density signal.

Contract declared as schema data with built-in defaults per type; pm validate reports per-type completeness violations; warn/require follows governance policy; custom types extend via schema; negative-control fixture in CI proves a malformed item fails
Make item well-formedness a declared, machine-checked contract per type and lifecycle stage
Agents can trust that any Epic has a charter and any Decision has consequences; completeness becomes a scoring signal instead of a hope
